# About this script

**Preregistered analysis (main text; RQ3).** Joint models of individual
stability across MIDUS 2 and MIDUS 3 in (3a) average daily sleep duration
and (3b) day-to-day sleep variability. Both are unconditional-means models
(plus the `weekend` control retained in all models) fit to the
participants in the full-time, standard-shift samples of both waves.
Run the MIDUS 2 and MIDUS 3 structuring scripts first.

Both models use 4000 iterations (2000 warmup) and `adapt_delta = 0.99`.
An earlier version of Model 3a had bulk ESS < 1000 at the preregistered
2000 iterations, so its iterations were doubled.

# Packages, data, and helper functions

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(brms)

M2_sample <- readRDS("../midus_2/M2_analysis_data_fulltime_standard.rds")
M3_sample <- readRDS("../midus_3/M3_analysis_data_fulltime_standard.rds")

model_output_dir <- "model_fits_cross_wave"
dir.create(model_output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Prereg convergence criteria: R-hat < 1.01, bulk and tail ESS > 1000,
# and 0 divergent transitions (population-level, SD, and correlation
# parameters)
check_convergence <- function(fit) {
  draws_summary <- posterior::summarise_draws(
    as_draws_df(fit, variable = "^(b_|sd_|cor_|sigma$)", regex = TRUE),
    "rhat", "ess_bulk", "ess_tail"
  )

  tibble(
    max_rhat = max(draws_summary$rhat, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_bulk_ess = min(draws_summary$ess_bulk, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_tail_ess = min(draws_summary$ess_tail, na.rm = TRUE),
    divergent = sum(nuts_params(fit, pars = "divergent__")$Value)
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      meets_prereg = max_rhat < 1.01 & min_bulk_ess > 1000 &
        min_tail_ess > 1000 & divergent == 0
    )
}

# Prereg assumption check: Q-Q plot of level-1 residuals
check_residual_normality <- function(fit, label) {
  resid_est <- residuals(
    fit,
    method = "posterior_predict"
  )[, "Estimate"]

  qqnorm(
    resid_est,
    main = paste0(label, ": Level-1 residual Q-Q plot")
  )

  qqline(resid_est)
}

# Both samples are already restricted to full-time, standard shift
stopifnot(
  all(M2_sample$is_fulltime == 1),
  all(M2_sample$is_standard_shift == 1),
  all(M3_sample$is_fulltime == 1),
  all(M3_sample$is_standard_shift == 1)
)
```

# Building the MIDUS 2 / MIDUS 3 panel

Only participants in both waves are included (prereg; MIDUS 2
participants who did not return are assumed missing at random). MIDUS 3
participants keep their MIDUS 2 `id`.

```{r}
panel_ids <- intersect(unique(M2_sample$id), unique(M3_sample$id))

M2_panel <- M2_sample %>% filter(id %in% panel_ids)
M3_panel <- M3_sample %>% filter(id %in% panel_ids)

cat(
  "Full-time/standard-shift participants:\n",
  "  MIDUS 2:", n_distinct(M2_sample$id), "\n",
  "  MIDUS 3:", n_distinct(M3_sample$id), "\n",
  "  In both waves (the panel):", length(panel_ids), "\n"
)

long_data <- bind_rows(
  M2_panel %>%
    transmute(id, weekend, sleep_next_night_minutes, wave = 1),
  M3_panel %>%
    transmute(id, weekend, sleep_next_night_minutes, wave = 2)
)

long_data$wave <- factor(
  long_data$wave,
  levels = c(1, 2),
  labels = c("MIDUS2", "MIDUS3")
)

# QC: rows per wave; every panel participant appears in both waves
table(long_data$wave, useNA = "ifany")

long_data %>%
  distinct(id, wave) %>%
  count(id) %>%
  count(n, name = "n_participants")
```

# Panel sample description

The panel is used only in this script, so it is described here. Age and
sex are at the participant level; sleep is at the diary-day level.

```{r}
panel_by_wave <- bind_rows(
  MIDUS2 = M2_panel,
  MIDUS3 = M3_panel,
  .id = "wave"
)

# Participant level: age at each wave, and sex
panel_by_wave %>%
  distinct(wave, id, age, sex) %>%
  group_by(wave) %>%
  summarise(
    participants = n(),
    age_mean = mean(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    age_sd = sd(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    age_min = min(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    age_max = max(age, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_female = sum(sex == 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    percent_female = mean(sex == 1, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Diary-day level: sleep, with between-person SD (SD of person means) and
# within-person SD (SD of deviations from each person's own mean)
panel_by_wave %>%
  filter(!is.na(sleep_next_night_minutes)) %>%
  group_by(wave, id) %>%
  mutate(
    person_mean = mean(sleep_next_night_minutes),
    deviation = sleep_next_night_minutes - person_mean
  ) %>%
  group_by(wave) %>%
  summarise(
    sleep_observations = n(),
    sleep_mean = mean(sleep_next_night_minutes),
    sleep_sd = sd(sleep_next_night_minutes),
    sleep_median = median(sleep_next_night_minutes),
    between_person_sd = sd(person_mean[!duplicated(id)]),
    within_person_sd = sd(deviation)
  ) %>%
  as.data.frame()
```

# Model 3a: stability of average daily sleep duration

Each wave gets its own mean (`0 + wave`). The two waves' random
intercepts are allowed to correlate, and that correlation is the
stability estimate. Because Model 1b (random scale) fit better than
Model 1a in both waves, 3a uses that formulation (prereg): each person
also has a wave-specific random scale on `sigma`. The scale effects are
uncorrelated here (`||`); their correlations, including the cross-wave
variability correlation, are what Model 3b adds.

```{r}
bf_model_3a <- bf(
  sleep_next_night_minutes ~ 0 + wave + weekend + (0 + wave | id),
  sigma ~ 0 + wave + (0 + wave || id)
)

fit_3a <- brm(
  bf_model_3a,
  data = long_data,
  family = gaussian(),
  chains = 4,
  # Iterations doubled per prereg (bulk ESS < 1000 at 2000 iterations)
  iter = 4000,
  warmup = 2000,
  seed = 2026,
  save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
  file = file.path(model_output_dir, "model_3a_stability_m2_m3"),
  file_refit = "never"
)

summary(fit_3a, prob = 0.9)

# Random-intercept correlation (90% credible interval)
vc_3a <- VarCorr(
  fit_3a,
  probs = c(0.05, 0.95)
)

vc_3a$id$cor["waveMIDUS2", c("Estimate", "Q5", "Q95"), "waveMIDUS3"]
```

# Model 3b: stability of day-to-day sleep variability

Adds a person- and wave-specific random scale to `sigma`. The shared `c`
tag correlates all four random effects; the MIDUS 2 scale vs. MIDUS 3
scale correlation is the stability of day-to-day variability.

```{r}
bf_model_3b <- bf(
  sleep_next_night_minutes ~ 0 + wave + weekend + (0 + wave | c | id),
  sigma ~ 0 + wave + (0 + wave | c | id)
)

fit_3b <- brm(
  bf_model_3b,
  data = long_data,
  family = gaussian(),
  chains = 4,
  iter = 4000,
  warmup = 2000,
  seed = 2026,
  save_pars = save_pars(all = TRUE),
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
  file = file.path(model_output_dir, "model_3b_stability_m2_m3"),
  file_refit = "never"
)

summary(fit_3b, prob = 0.9)

vc_3b <- VarCorr(
  fit_3b,
  probs = c(0.05, 0.95)
)

# Full 4 x 4 correlation matrix (point estimates)
vc_3b$id$cor[, "Estimate", ]

# Stability in average sleep (90% credible interval)
vc_3b$id$cor["waveMIDUS2", c("Estimate", "Q5", "Q95"), "waveMIDUS3"]

# Stability in day-to-day sleep variability (90% credible interval)
vc_3b$id$cor["sigma_waveMIDUS2", c("Estimate", "Q5", "Q95"), "sigma_waveMIDUS3"]
```

# Model diagnostics (prereg convergence and residual checks)

```{r}
models <- list(
  fit_3a = fit_3a,
  fit_3b = fit_3b
)

sapply(models, nobs)

# Convergence: every row should show meets_prereg = TRUE
bind_rows(lapply(models, check_convergence), .id = "model")
```

```{r}
for (model_name in names(models)) {
  check_residual_normality(models[[model_name]], model_name)
}
```
